invariants.statement: The optimisation problem is to minimise f(x) over x in R^d, and a differentiable local minimiser x* satisfies πf(x*) = 0.
For a potential-energy function V(q), the force is F(q) = -dV/dq(q), so equilibrium corresponds to dV/dq(q) = 0.
A differentiable function is L-smooth when ||∇f(x) - ∇f(y)|| <= L||x - y|| for all x,y.
If f is L-smooth, then f(y) <= f(x) + <∇f(x), y-x> + (L/2)||y-x||^2.
A differentiable function is convex if f(y) >= f(x) + <∇f(x), y-x> for all x,y.
A differentiable function is μ-strongly convex if f(y) >= f(x) + <∇f(x), y-x> + (μ/2)||y-x||^2 for all x,y with μ > 0.
Gradient descent uses x_{k+1} = x_k - α_k ∇f(x_k), where α_k > 0 is the step size.
conditions: current point x_k and gradient at x_k are known

invariants.statement: A backtracking step is accepted when f(x_k - α_k ∇f(x_k)) <= f(x_k) - cα_k||∇f(x_k)||^2 with 0 < c < 1/2.
For an L-smooth convex function and constant step size 1/L, gradient descent satisfies f(x_k) - f(x*) <= L||x_0 - x*||^2/(2k).
For an L-smooth μ-strongly convex function, gradient descent with step size 1/L can achieve f(x_k) - f(x*) <= (1 - μ/L)^k (f(x_0) - f(x*)).
conditions: f is L-smooth and μ-strongly convex

invariants.statement: Momentum uses x_{k+1} = x_k - α∇f(x_k) + β(x_k - x_{k-1}) with β in [0,1).
Stochastic gradient descent uses x_{k+1} = x_k - η_k g_k(x_k), where g_k(x_k) is an unbiased estimate of the gradient.
conditions: step sizes satisfy the Robbins-Monro conditions
